_note: THE COLONY MANAGEMENT SCREEN'S GEOMETRY, AND THE ONLY PLACE IT IS TYPED. Every rectangle is in the 1920x1080 reference space (core/layout.py). tools/frame_mask.py reads this file and renders one mask per supported resolution; the frame artwork is drawn from the 1080p mask, tools/frame_holes.py derives the cutout boxes from the artwork, and a smoke check asserts holes == mask == boxes.json at every resolution (decision 3). So a rectangle changes HERE and nowhere else, and everything downstream is generated - decision 1 and decision 40. These are Data's design inputs of 6 September 2026; where a number is derived rather than chosen, the derivation is in the _*_note beside it.
_bezel_note: The metal border outside every window. 36 reference px at 1080p. It is not a rectangle in the list below because nothing is drawn into it - it is what the frame artwork occupies where no window is cut.
_list_columns_note: 300 + 394*3 + 314 + 36 = 1832, which is the list's own width exactly - the columns are the list, with no slack to distribute (contrast the old single-track row, where six floor divisions dropped pixels that had to be given to the name column). PROVISIONAL until doc/pop_stacking.md's open questions are closed: the figure columns must fit at least as many unsquished figures as the original's 128 px does at the chosen figure scale. THE BUILDING COLUMN IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN: the original prints the producing text with BILL::Squeeze_Print_Formatted_Paragraph_(0x200, y, 0x55, 0x16, ...) at colsum.cpp:621 - 85 px of a 640 px screen, 13.3 % - and 13.3 % of 1832 is 244. 314 is wider than the transcription requires; the surplus is the extra HD width that Data's Stage 1 decision sends to the column reservation rather than to wider figure spacing. See colonybuild.py for why the width is a RESERVATION and never a squeeze target.
_lower_band_note: Four boxes, flush at 44 on the left and 1876 on the right, with EQUAL gaps of 18. Making them equal cost two pixels and they came from planet_output: 1920 - 88 of margin - 320 - 883 - 253 - 320 leaves 56 for three gaps and 56 is not divisible by 3, so equal gaps need the content to move by 1 or 2 px. planet_output took it because it is the only width in the band that is not fixed by something else - the two 320s are a pair and 253 is locked by the inset's aspect (see _galaxy_inset_note). 44 + 320 + 18 + 885 + 18 + 253 + 18 + 320 = 1876. The gaps were 12, 12 and 32 until 7 September 2026, which was flush at both ends and put the inset 20 px left of where an even band puts it. The inset is 20 px shorter than its neighbours and is centred against them (776 + (220-200)/2 = 786), because its height is fixed by its own aspect and not by the band.
_galaxy_inset_note: 253 x 200 IS DERIVED AND CONFIRMED - doc/colony_inset_geometry.md Part 3. The original's inset covers 50.6*M x 40*M world units, whose aspect is 1.2651 at EVERY galaxy size because both divisors are constants and M cancels (movebox.cpp:20-21). 253/200 = 1.2650 against that, so the crop fills the box with no letterbox at any size INCLUDING orion2re's Maximum - the earlier expectation that Maximum letterboxes is WITHDRAWN, and it only did so if the crop were the galaxy rather than the original's coverage. The scale that follows is exactly 5/M reference px per world unit. At 3840x2160 the box is 506 x 400 device px, which is the small galaxy's own world extent at 1:1.
_figure_scale_note: INTEGER STEPS, and that is the whole reason the table exists. A population figure is 28 x 28 native px (RACEICON.LBX, every people entry), and the layout scales are 1, 4/3 and 2 - so proportional scaling would want 2, 2.667 and 4, and 2.667 is not an integer. Nearest-neighbour at a fractional step invents pixels the original does not have, which a reference figure may not do. 2 / 3 / 4 gives 56 / 84 / 112 px. The list height of 660 assumes the 1080p step is 2; at 3 the list grows and the lower band shrinks, and THIS FILE is the only place that changes. Marked HD EXTENSION in core/zoomtables.py.
